html:
Runit Dome is a concrete cap on Runit Island, in Enewetak Atoll, over a bomb crater filled with radioactive soil and debris from US nuclear tests. It was built from 1977 to 1980.

The United States tested dozens of bombs at Enewetak between 1948 and 1958. During the cleanup, soldiers scraped up contaminated soil and dumped it in the crater; the bottom was never lined.

The dome has cracked, and scientists fear rising seas and storms may break it open, releasing waste into the lagoon. People of Enewetak returned to other islets of the atoll in 1980. Compare Castle Bravo and the Compact, and sea level rise.
